headline: Council approves wildfire lawsuit settlement, refers housing and water bills to committees

meeting.voteItem: County Communication 24-23, proposed amendment to Bill 87
meeting.summary: The council approved a committee's recommended global settlement of County wildfire lawsuits from August 2023, with twice-yearly lawyer reports on future cases. It sent Bills 103 and 104 to Housing and Land Use and Bill 106 to Water and Infrastructure.
meeting.recap: All nine council members were present.[[0:02:40]] A committee recommended a global settlement of all County wildfire lawsuits from August 2023.[[1:32:05]] The committee had met in executive session (a closed-door discussion) with its lawyers.[[1:33:03]] The council approved the settlement recommendation.[[1:34:59]] The council filled a Board of Ethics vacancy, nine ayes to zero.[[1:39:28]] Bills 103 and 104, on housing density and kitchenettes, went to a housing committee.[[1:46:13]] Bill 106, on private water systems, went to the Water and Infrastructure Committee.[[1:47:08]] Bill 108, creating a passport application fund, passed first reading, nine ayes to zero.[[1:49:07]] Bill 87 lets temporary structures allowed under an emergency proclamation stay up to five years.[[1:59:47]] Bill 96, exempting storage shipping containers in industrial zones from building permits, passed.[[2:05:29]] An amendment lets $500,000 for the wildfire one-year commemoration also pay for a memorial.[[2:07:23]]
decided: The council postponed this item until it took up Bill 87.
The council sent Bills 103 and 104 to the Housing and Land Use Committee.
The council sent Bill 105 to the Housing and Land Use Committee.
The council sent Bill 106 to the Water and Infrastructure Committee.
The council sent Bill 107 to the Efficiency Solutions and Circular Systems Committee.
The council sent Bill 111 to committee.
meeting.next: The County's lawyers must send the council a twice-yearly report on future cases settled under the settlement resolution.

issues.oneLine: Bill 106, on regional consolidation and acquisition of private water systems, was sent to the Water and Infrastructure Committee.
issues.why: A testifier said the water department may find there is not enough water for a subdivision if more houses are allowed on each lot.
issues.brief: A resolution approving a director for the East Maui Regional Water Authority was sent to committee.[[#1]]

issues.oneLine: Bills 103 and 104, on housing density and kitchenettes, were sent to the Housing and Land Use Committee.
issues.why: A testifier said Bill 103 could double, triple or even quadruple housing density in R1, R2 and R3 zoning.
issues.brief: A testifier said Bill 104 could turn single-family homes into three-family dwellings.[[#1]] The testifier asked that water, wastewater, public works and fire agencies comment on the bills before they return to committee.[[#2]] The testifier warned the bills could be used by developers to create second homes.[[#3]] Another testifier said Bills 87, 105 and 110 would help provide temporary housing.[[#4]]

issues.oneLine: The council is acting on a global settlement of wildfire lawsuits against the County from the August 2023 wildfires.
issues.why: A member said she hopes the settlement brings closure and comfort to the fire victims.
issues.next: The County's lawyers must report to the council twice a year on future cases settled under the resolution.
issues.brief: The committee amended the resolution so the settlement covers claims from the Lahaina and Upcountry wildfires.[[#1]] The committee voted 6-0 to recommend adopting the settlement resolution.[[#2]] Bill 87 lets temporary structures allowed under an emergency proclamation stay up to five years.[[#3]]
